note: Regular season: no game ended tied and overtime goals came as late as the 17th minute, so overtime ran until a goal; its period length is not recorded. Unconfirmed by a source.
Overtime goals as late as the 20th minute, never two in a game, and tied games when nobody scored. Unconfirmed by a source.
Overtime goals only up to the 10th minute, never two in a game, 37 ties. Unconfirmed by a source.
A non-sudden-death 10-minute period, played in full (up to 4 overtime goals in one game), eliminated from 1942-11-21 during 1942-43. The 1928-29 start is observed, not stated by the source.
No regular-season overtime: tied after 60 minutes is a tie, through 1982-83.
5-minute 5-on-5 sudden-death overtime from 1983-84; a tie if nobody scored.
4 skaters a side from 1999-2000, when the overtime-loss point also began (NHL.com; confirmed by the owner 2026-11-13). One Wikipedia page says 2000-01. 2004-05 was not played.
Shootout from 2005-06 if still tied; no more ties.
3 skaters a side from 2015-16 (adopted 2015-06-24), then a shootout.

Playoffs: 20-minute sudden-death periods until a goal, at full strength, no shootout. The source states the current format; the play-by-play shows it from 1918-19 (never two overtime goals, goals to the 20th minute, up to 6 overtime periods). A few playoff games before the 1950s ended tied after overtime (unexplained here). The 2019-20 seeding round-robin used regular-season overtime and shootouts.
